1.word_for_word: द्वादशे तु — in the twelfth chapter; महा-सर्प-वपुर्-धरम् अघासुरम् — Aghāsura, who assumed the body of a great serpent; वत्स-पाल-गिलम् — who swallowed the calf-herd boys; क्रुद्धः गले अहन् — He, angered, killed him in the throat; महा-बक-गल-क्रीडा केवलस्य न कौतुकम् — mere play in the throat of the great Baka was no wonder for Him; इतीव अघासुर-मुखे स-सखः प्राविशत् हरिः — as if for that reason Hari entered Aghāsura’s mouth with His friends; क्वचित् कदाचित् वनाशाय — on one occasion, for going to the forest; वन एव प्रथमं भोजनं कर्तुम् — to take the first meal there in the forest itself.
1.translation: In the twelfth chapter Aghāsura, who had assumed the body of a huge serpent and swallowed the calf-herd boys, is described as being slain by the angry Lord in his throat. As though play within the throat of the great Baka had been no marvel for Him, Hari entered Aghāsura’s mouth together with His friends. On one occasion, when they went to the forest, the intention was to take their first meal there in the forest itself.

2.word_for_word: तेन एव शृङ्ग-रवेण — by that very sound of the horn; श्री-कृष्णेन वा सह — or together with Śrī Kṛṣṇa; पृथुकाः बालाः — the little boys; स्निग्धाः स्नेह-युक्ताः — affectionate, endowed with love; शिक् शिक्यम् — śik means a sling/netted carrier; रम्या शिग्-वेत्रादयः येषां ते — those whose slings, sticks and the like were charming; सहस्राधिक-सङ्ख्या-युक्तान् वत्सान् — calves numbering more than a thousand.
2.translation: They went by the very sound of the horn, or together with Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ‘Pṛthukāḥ’ means the little boys, and ‘snigdhāḥ’ means affectionate. ‘Śik’ means a sling or carrying-net. Their slings, herding sticks and other implements were charming, and the calves numbered more than a thousand.

3.word_for_word: पूर्व-श्लोकस्य व्याख्या — the explanation of the preceding verse; द्रष्टव्या — is to be consulted.
3.translation: The explanation of this verse is to be understood from the commentary on the preceding verse.

4.word_for_word: काच-आदिभिः पूर्वं मातृभिः भूषिताः अपि — although their mothers had already adorned them with glass ornaments and the like; फल-आदिभिः आत्मानम् अभूषयन् — they further decorated themselves with fruits and similar forest objects.
4.translation: Although their mothers had already adorned them with ornaments such as glass bangles, the boys decorated themselves again with fruits and other things found in the forest.

5.translation: ‘Muṣṇantaḥ’ means that they were stealing or taking one another’s things away.

6.word_for_word: यदि दूरं गतः कृष्णः भवति — if Kṛṣṇa had gone far away; तर्हि — then.
6.translation: The sense is: if Kṛṣṇa happened to have gone far away, then they would act as the verse describes.

7.word_for_word: ध्मान्तः — blowing; वादयन्तः — sounding; भृङ्गैः सह — together with the bees.
7.translation: ‘Dhmāntaḥ’ means blowing or sounding their instruments, in accompaniment with the humming bees.

8.word_for_word: विच्छायाभिः — with moving shadows; पक्षि-च्छायाभिः — with the shadows of birds; कलापिभिः — with the crested ones; मयूरैः — peacocks.
8.translation: ‘Vicchāyābhiḥ’ refers to the shadows of the birds, and ‘kalāpibhiḥ’ means the peacocks.

9.word_for_word: कीश-बालान् — young monkeys; वृक्ष-शाखासु लम्बमानानि वानर-लाङ्गूलानि आकर्षन्तः — pulling the monkeys’ tails hanging from tree branches; लाङ्गूलम् अमुञ्चन्तः — not letting go of the tail; तैः सह द्रुमान् आरोहन्तः — climbing the trees with them; विकुर्वन्तः — making faces and gestures; दन्त-दर्शन-भ्रू-विजृम्भादिभिः — by showing the teeth, moving the brows and the like; पलाशिषु वृक्षेषु प्लवन्तः — leaping among leafy trees; शाखायाः शाखान्तरम् उद्गच्छन्तः — going from one branch to another.
9.translation: The boys pulled the tails of young monkeys as they hung from the branches and, without letting go, climbed the trees with them. They imitated the monkeys’ grimaces by showing their teeth, moving their eyebrows and making other expressions, and leapt through the leafy trees from one branch to another.

10.word_for_word: प्रतिच्छायाः — reflected shadows; प्रतिबिम्बानि — reflections or images.
10.translation: ‘Praticchāyāḥ’ means their reflected images or reflections.

11.word_for_word: तान् अतिविस्मितः श्लोक-द्वयेन अभिनन्दति — greatly astonished, he praises them in two verses; सतां विदुषां ब्रह्म च तत्-सुखं च अनुभूतिः — for the wise saints, He is Brahman and the experience of its bliss; स्व-प्रकाश-परम-सुखेन — as self-luminous supreme bliss; भक्तानां पर-दैवतेन आत्म-प्रदेन नाथेन — for devotees, He is the supreme deity, the Lord who gives Himself; मायाश्रितानां नर-दारकतया प्रतीयमानेन — to those under māyā He appears merely as a human child; सह विजह्रुः — they sported with Him; कृतानां पुण्यानां पुञ्जाः राशयः येषां ते — they possessed heaps upon heaps of accumulated merit; ब्रह्म-विदां तद्-अनुभवः एव — knowers of Brahman merely experience Him; भक्तानाम् अतिगौरवेण एव भजनम् — devotees worship Him with profound reverence; एते तु तेन सह सख्येन विजह्रुः — but these boys sported with Him in friendship; अहो भाग्यम् — what astonishing fortune!.
11.translation: Astonished beyond measure, Śuka praises the boys in two verses. For the wise saints, Kṛṣṇa is Brahman itself and the experience of its self-luminous supreme bliss. For devotees He is the supreme Deity, the Lord who gives Himself; to those sheltered in māyā He appears merely as a human boy. Yet these children sported with Him. They were therefore persons in whom heaps of accumulated merit had gathered. Knowers of Brahman merely experience Him, and devotees worship Him with profound reverence; these boys, however, played with Him as friends. Such was their astonishing good fortune.

12.word_for_word: बहु-जन्मभिः — through many births; कृच्छ्रेण — with great difficulty; धृतः आत्मा मनः यैः — by those whose mind has been restrained; तैः अपि — even by such persons.
12.translation: The reference is even to those who, after many births and with great difficulty, have succeeded in restraining the mind.

13.word_for_word: सुख-क्रीडन-वीक्षणेन क्षमा यस्य सः — He for whom the sight of their happy play was pleasing/forbearing; यस्य अन्तः अन्तरं छिद्रं — whose inner opening; पीतामृतैः अपि अमरैः — even by the gods who have drunk nectar; मृत्यु-भीतैः प्रतीक्ष्यते — is watched by those still afraid of death; कथं मरिष्यति कदा वा — wondering how and when death may come; यद् वा — alternatively; सुख-क्रीडनम् — the delightful play; यद् अन्तर्-हृदये अमरैः प्रतीक्ष्यते — which the gods contemplate within their hearts; पुनर् निज-जीवितेप्सुभिः — still desirous of preserving their own lives; न अमृत-पान-मात्रेण जीवनं स-फलं भवति — life is not made fruitful merely by drinking nectar; भगवल्-लीला-अनुस्मरणेन — but by remembering Bhagavān’s līlā.
13.translation: One reading describes the gods, though drinkers of nectar, as still watching the serpent’s inner opening in fear of death and wondering how and when the danger would end. Alternatively, the point is that even the immortal gods, still desiring true life, contemplate this delightful play within their hearts. Mere drinking of nectar does not make life fruitful; life becomes fruitful through remembrance of Bhagavān’s līlā. Therefore this līlā is what they continually contemplate within.

14.word_for_word: कृष्ण-प्रमुखान् अर्भकान् दृष्ट्वा — seeing the boys headed by Kṛṣṇa; स इति व्यवस्य निश्चित्य — deciding firmly concerning Him; अजगरं वपुः धृत्वा — assuming the body of a python; तेषां ग्रसन-आशया पथि व्यशेत — he lay on the path intending to swallow them; कंसेन अनुशिष्टः प्रहितः — instructed and sent by Kaṃsa; बकी पूतना — Bakī is Pūtanā; मम तयोर् द्वयोः सोदरयोः स्थाने — in place of those two, my brother and sister; एनं कृष्णं स-बलं स-सैन्यम् — this Kṛṣṇa, together with Balarāma and His whole force; वत्स-तत्-पाल-सहितम् — together with the calves and their keepers; हनिष्यामि — I shall kill.
14.translation: Seeing the boys headed by Kṛṣṇa, Aghāsura made his decision, assumed the body of a python, and lay across the path intending to swallow them. He had been instructed and sent by Kaṃsa. ‘Bakī’ means Pūtanā. Aghāsura’s resolve was: ‘In place of those two siblings of mine, I shall kill this Kṛṣṇa together with Balarāma and His entire force—the calves and the boys who tend them.’

15.word_for_word: ननु तथापि व्रज-स्थाः तु अवशिष्येरन् — objection: even then those remaining in Vraja would survive; एत इति आह — he answers with ‘these’; तिलापः कृताः — reduced to an offering of sesame-water for the dead; तिलोदकतया कल्पिताः — counted as already dead; वर्ष्मसु — in the bodies; देहेषु — in their bodies; प्रजाः एव असवः येषां ते — those whose very life-breaths are their offspring.
15.translation: An objection arises: even if the boys are killed, the people remaining in Vraja would survive. Aghāsura answers by speaking of ‘these’ children as though they were already reduced to the sesame-water offering made for the dead. ‘In their bodies’ means in their physical forms, and the elders are those whose very life-breaths are their children; if the children die, the elders will die as well.

16.word_for_word: योजनायामम् — a yojana in extent; योजन-प्रमाणेन दैर्घ्येण युक्तम् — possessing a length measured by a yojana; महाद्रिवत् पीवरम् — massive like a great mountain; व्यात्तम् प्रसारितम् — opened wide, stretched out; गुहा-तुल्यम् आननम् — a mouth like a cave.
16.translation: His body extended for a yojana and was massive like a great mountain. His mouth was stretched wide open like a cavern.

17.word_for_word: अद्भुतम् इति यद् उक्तम् तद् दर्शयितुं विशिनष्टि — he gives particulars to show why it was called astonishing; धरायाम् अधरोष्ठः — his lower lip lay upon the earth; जलदेषु उत्तरोष्ठः — his upper lip reached the clouds; दर्यौ इव आननस्य अन्तौ सृक्किणी — the corners of his mouth were like mountain caves; गिरेः शृङ्गाणि इव दंष्ट्राः — his fangs were like mountain peaks; ध्वान्तवत् अन्तरास्यम् — the inside of his mouth was like darkness; वितत-अध्ववत् जिह्वा — his tongue was like a broad road; परुष-अनिलवत् श्वासः — his breath was like a harsh wind; दववत् ईक्षणयोः उष्णः — the heat of his glance was like a forest fire.
17.translation: To show why the form was called astonishing, Śrīdhara specifies its features: the lower lip rested upon the earth and the upper lip reached the clouds; the corners of the mouth resembled mountain caverns and the fangs mountain peaks. The inside was dark as night, the tongue stretched out like a broad road, the breath blew like a harsh wind, and the heat of his gaze was like a forest fire.

18.word_for_word: वस्तुतः अजगरम् एव व्यात्त-तुण्डं दृष्ट्वा — though they were actually seeing a python with its mouth open; वृन्दावनस्य श्रीः सम्पत् एषा इति भ्रान्त्या मत्वा — mistakenly taking it to be a magnificent feature of Vṛndāvana; विपरीतम् उत्प्रेक्षितवन्तः — they imagined the reverse of the truth; व्यात्त-अजगर-तुण्ड-सादृश्येन — by its resemblance to the open mouth of a python.
18.translation: They were in fact looking directly at a python with its mouth open, but in their confusion they took it for one of the splendid sights of Vṛndāvana. Thus, because the landscape resembled the gaping mouth of a python, they imagined the reality in reverse.

19.word_for_word: उत्प्रेक्षाम् एव प्रश्नोत्तराभ्याम् आहुः — by questions and answers they voiced their conjecture; सत्त्व-कूटम् — an imitation or semblance of a living creature; इदं वा न वा — is this such a thing or not?; अस्मत् सङ्ग्रसनाय — for swallowing all of us; व्यात्तं व्याल-तुण्डं तद्वत् आचरति वा न वा — does this gaping serpent-mouth behave as though meant for that, or not?.
19.translation: The boys expressed their conjecture through questions and answers: ‘Is this merely an imitation of a living serpent, or not? And does this gaping serpent-mouth really look as though it has opened in order to swallow all of us, or does it not?’

20.word_for_word: निश्चितं तथैव इति आहुः — they concluded that it was indeed so; अर्क-करैः आरक्तं घनम् — a cloud reddened by the rays of the sun; उत्तरोष्ठवत् पश्यत — look at it as though it were the upper lip; तस्य घनस्य प्रतिच्छायया अरुणं रोधः-स्थलम् — the ground reddened by the reflection of that cloud; अधरोष्ठवत् पश्यत — look at it as the lower lip; पश्यत इति सर्वत्र अन्वेति — the word ‘look’ is to be supplied throughout.
20.translation: They then affirmed their conjecture: ‘Yes, it is just like that. Look at the cloud reddened by the sun’s rays as its upper lip, and at the ground made red by the cloud’s reflection as its lower lip.’ The imperative ‘look’ is to be understood with each item in the description.

21.word_for_word: सृक्किभ्याम् — with the two corners of the lips; ओष्ठ-प्रान्ताभ्याम् — with the ends of the lips; प्रतिस्पर्धेते — they rival; तुल्यतया वर्तेते — they stand in equality; नगोदरे — clefts within the mountain; गिरि-दर्यौ — mountain caves; एताः तुङ्ग-शृङ्गालयः — these lofty peak-formations; तस्य दंष्ट्राभिः स्पर्धमानाः — rival his fangs.
21.translation: The mountain clefts on either side seemed to rival the two corners of the serpent’s lips, and the lofty mountain peaks seemed to compete with his fangs.

22.word_for_word: आस्तृत-आयाम-मार्गः — a road spread out at great length; विस्तृतः दैर्घ्यवान् मार्गः — a broad, long road; प्रतिगर्जति — rivals or answers; एषां शृङ्गाणाम् अन्तर्-गतं ध्वान्तम् — the darkness lying between these peaks; एतद् अन्तर्-आननम् — the interior of this mouth; प्रति गर्जति — resembles/rivals it.
22.translation: The long, broad road resembled the extended tongue. The darkness lying between the mountain peaks seemed to rival the darkness within the serpent’s mouth.

23.word_for_word: दावेन उष्णः खरः वातः अयम् — this harsh wind is hot from the forest fire; तेन दावाग्निना दग्धानां सत्त्वानां दुर्गन्धः — the foul smell of creatures burned by that fire; स एव सर्प-अन्तर्-गत-आमिष-गन्धवत् भाति — appears like the smell of flesh inside a serpent.
23.translation: The harsh wind was hot because of a forest fire, and the foul odor of creatures burned by that fire seemed like the smell of flesh lying within a serpent’s belly.

24.word_for_word: एवं सन्तम् एव अजगरम् अन्यथा उत्प्रेक्ष्य — thus imagining the real python to be something else; निर्भयाः ययुः — they went forward without fear; किं ग्रसिता ग्रसिष्यति — if it is a swallower, will it swallow us?; अनेन श्री-कृष्णेन हन्त्रा — when this slayer, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is here; बकारेः — of the enemy of Baka; उशत् कमनीयं मुखम् — the lovely, charming face.
24.translation: Thus they misimagined the very real python as something else and advanced without fear. Their thought was: ‘Even if it is a creature that swallows, will it really swallow us while Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of Baka, is here?’ They looked toward the charming face of Baka’s enemy.

25.word_for_word: अमृषा — not false, actually real; वस्तुतः सर्प-वपुः असुरः एव — in reality it was the demon in a serpent body; मृषायते — it was being taken as unreal; स्वानां सर्प-सादृश्य-गोचरत्वेन प्रतीयते — it appeared to His companions merely as something resembling a serpent; तान् निरोद्धुं वारयितुं यावत् मनः दधे — while Kṛṣṇa formed the intention to restrain and stop them; तावत् प्रविष्टाः — by then they had entered.
25.translation: The serpent-form was not imaginary at all: it really was the demon. Yet to Kṛṣṇa’s companions it appeared merely as something resembling a serpent, and thus they took the real thing for an imitation. By the time Kṛṣṇa resolved to restrain them and keep them back, they had already entered.

26.word_for_word: तावत् प्रविष्टाः एव केवलम् — they had merely entered by then; न तु तेन गीर्णाः गिलिताः — they had not yet been swallowed by him; जीर्णाः इति पाठे अपि सः एव अर्थः — even with the reading jīrṇāḥ the sense is the same; हतयोः स्वकयोः अन्तं स्मरति अनुध्यायति — he remembered and pondered the fate of his own two slain siblings; बकारेः श्री-कृष्णस्य प्रवेशं प्रतीक्षमाणेन — therefore he waited for Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Baka’s enemy, to enter.
26.translation: At that point the boys had only entered; the serpent had not yet swallowed them. Even if the text is read ‘jīrṇāḥ,’ the intended sense is the same. Aghāsura remembered and brooded over the fate of his two slain siblings and therefore waited for Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Baka, to enter as well.

27.word_for_word: स्व-करात् अवच्युतान् विनिःसृतान् — those who had slipped out from His own hand/protection and gone inside; विस्मितः सन् — being astonished; कृत्यं किम् अत्र इति विचिन्त्य — considering, ‘What is to be done here?’; तत्र उपायं ज्ञात्वा — recognizing the means; स्वयम् अपि अविशत् — He Himself also entered.
27.translation: Seeing His companions go in after slipping beyond His immediate protection, Kṛṣṇa was astonished and considered, ‘What is to be done here?’ Having discerned the means of saving them, He Himself entered the serpent.

28.word_for_word: कथं विचिन्त्य — how did He deliberate?; अस्य जीवनम् — the life of this demon; अमीषां च विहिंसनम् — and the destruction of these boys; इति द्वयं निश्चितं कथं न स्यात् — how can these two results both be prevented/settled?.
28.translation: What did He deliberate? He considered how the two opposed outcomes—the demon’s continued life and the destruction of these boys—could both be decisively prevented.

29.word_for_word: घन-च्छदाः — covered by clouds; मेघ-अन्तरिताः — hidden behind clouds; कौणपाः — Rākṣasas; कूणपाशिनः राक्षसाः — corpse-eating demons; कोणपः निरृतिः तदीयाः इति वा — alternatively, those belonging to Nirṛti, called Kauṇapa.
29.translation: ‘Ghana-cchadāḥ’ means hidden behind clouds. ‘Kauṇapāḥ’ refers to the corpse-eating Rākṣasas, or alternatively to the followers of Nirṛti known as Kauṇapas.

30.word_for_word: चूर्णी-कर्तुम् इच्छोः तस्य — of the demon wishing to crush Him; गले आदौ एव — first of all in his throat; तरसा ववृधे — Kṛṣṇa rapidly expanded; अवर्धत — He grew.
30.translation: As the demon sought to crush Him, Kṛṣṇa first of all expanded rapidly within his throat.

31.word_for_word: निरुद्धः मुखादीनां मार्ग-भूतः कण्ठः यस्य — whose throat, the passage to the mouth and other outlets, had been blocked; उद्गीर्ण-दृष्टेः — whose eyes were forced outward; बहिर् निर्गत-लोचनस्य — whose eyeballs protruded; अन्तरङ्गे देह-मध्ये पूर्णः परिभृतः — the life-air became completely confined within the body; मूर्ध्नि ब्रह्म-रन्ध्रं निर्भिद्य — piercing the brahmarandhra at the crown; बहिः विनिर्गतः — it went out.
31.translation: His throat—the passage leading to the mouth and other outlets—was blocked, and his eyes were forced outward and protruded. His vital force, completely confined within the body, finally pierced the brahmarandhra at the crown of the head and escaped outside.

32.word_for_word: प्राणेषु — into the life-breaths; इन्द्रियेषु — into the senses; स्वया अमृत-वर्षिण्या दृष्ट्या एव — by His own glance, which showers nectar.
32.translation: Kṛṣṇa restored life to their vital airs and senses by His own glance, a glance that showers nectar.

33.word_for_word: अहि-देहे स्थितं शुद्ध-सत्त्वमयं ज्योतिः — the pure-sattva effulgence that had been in the serpent’s body; निर्गत्य खे अवस्थितम् — came out and remained in the sky; तस्मिन् ईशे विवेश — it entered that Lord.
33.translation: An effulgence of pure sattva emerged from the serpent’s body and remained in the sky; it then entered the Lord Himself.

34.word_for_word: स्व-कृतः — performed by themselves; स्व-कार्य-कृतः — arising from their own proper functions; श्री-कृष्णस्य अर्हणम् — worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; अकृत अकुर्वत — they performed it; पूजाम् अकुर्वन् — they offered worship; सुगाः — those who sing beautifully; सुष्ठु गायन्ति इति गन्धर्वादयः — Gandharvas and the like, so called because they sing well.
34.translation: Each celestial group offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa the worship appropriate to its own function. ‘Sugāḥ,’ those who sing beautifully, refers to the Gandharvas and similar celestial singers.

35.word_for_word: तेषां यानि अद्भुत-स्तोत्रादीनि — their marvelous praises and other celebrations; तेषां नैक-उत्सवाः मङ्गल-स्वनाः — the auspicious sounds of their many festivities; स्व-धाम्नः अन्ति समीपे श्रुत्वा — hearing them near his own abode; अजः ब्रह्मा अचिरात् आगतः — the unborn Brahmā soon came; ईशस्य श्री-कृष्णस्य महि महिमानं दृष्ट्वा — seeing the greatness of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa; विस्मयं प्राप — he became astonished.
35.translation: Hearing near his own abode the auspicious sounds of their many celebrations—their marvelous hymns and other festivities—the unborn Brahmā quickly came. Seeing the majesty of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he was filled with wonder.

36.word_for_word: बहु-तिथम् — for a long time; बहु-कालम् — for a lengthy period; आक्रीड-गह्वरम् — a cavern used for play; क्रीडार्थं महा-बिलम् — a great cave serving as a place of sport.
36.translation: ‘Bahu-titham’ means for a long time. The serpent’s body became an ‘ākrīḍa-gahvara,’ a great cavern used by the boys as a place of play.

37.word_for_word: अन्यत् च अति-चित्रं वृत्तम् — another exceedingly strange event occurred; कौमारं पञ्चमाब्दान्तम् — childhood extends to the end of the fifth year; पौगण्डं दशमावधि — boyhood extends to the tenth; कैशोरम् आ-पञ्चदशात् — adolescence to the fifteenth; हरेः कौमारजं पञ्चमाब्द-कृतं कर्म — Hari’s deed performed in His fifth year; तदा एव दृष्ट्वा — though they saw it then; पौगण्डके षष्ठे अब्दे — in His sixth year, the beginning of boyhood; अद्य एव एतद् वृत्तम् इति ऊचुः — they said, ‘This happened only today’; मृत्योः सकाशात् आत्मनाम् मोक्षणम् — the deliverance of themselves from death; अहेः च — and of the serpent; संसार-लक्षणात् — from the bondage characterized as saṃsāra; अघासुरस्य ज्योतिषः श्री-कृष्णे प्रवेशम् — the entrance of Aghāsura’s effulgence into Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
37.translation: Another exceedingly strange fact is now stated. Childhood extends through the fifth year, boyhood through the tenth, adolescence through the fifteenth, and youth thereafter. This deed of Hari occurred in His fifth year and the boys saw it then, yet in His sixth year they spoke as though it had happened only that very day. The deed was the rescue of themselves from literal death and the liberation of the serpent from the deathlike bondage of saṃsāra; they had also seen Aghāsura’s effulgence enter Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and only then related it.

38.word_for_word: न एतत् विचित्रम् — this is not astonishing; किं तत् इति अपेक्षायाम् — when one asks what is meant; अघः अपि इति — he answers with the words ‘even Agha’; आत्म-साम्यम् — equality with Himself; स्व-समान-रूपताम् — a form like His own.
38.translation: Śuka says that even this should not be regarded as astonishing. The words ‘even Agha’ show why: Aghāsura attained ‘equality with Himself,’ that is, a form resembling the Lord’s own.

39.word_for_word: यस्य अङ्गं मूर्तिः — whose bodily form; तस्य प्रतिमा प्रतिकृतिः — its image or replica; तत्र अपि केवलं मनो-मयी — even when that image exists only mentally; सा अपि बलात् अन्तर्-आहिता सती — when forcibly and steadily installed within the mind; भागवतीं गतिं ददौ प्रह्लादादिभ्यः — it bestowed the Lord’s destination upon Prahlāda and others; सः एव साक्षात् स्वयम् अन्तर्-गतः किं पुनः — how much more when the Lord Himself entered within directly; नित्या आत्म-सुख-अनुभूतिः — eternal experience of the bliss of the Self; तया अभितः व्युदस्ता माया येन सः — one by whom māyā is driven away on every side through that experience.
39.translation: Even a mere image or representation of the Lord’s form, when formed only in the mind and firmly installed within, bestowed the Lord’s own destination upon Prahlāda and others. How much more, then, when the Lord Himself personally entered within Aghāsura? The Lord eternally experiences the bliss of His own Self, and by that presence māyā is driven away completely.

40.word_for_word: येन श्रवणेन — by that hearing; निगृहीतं वशी-कृतं चेतः यस्य सः — one whose mind has been restrained and brought under control.
40.translation: The phrase describes one whose mind has been restrained and brought under control by hearing this narration.

41.word_for_word: कालान्तरे — at a later time; कौमारे कृतम् — what had been done in childhood; पौगण्डके — in boyhood; कथं ज्ञात्वा ऊचुः — how did they remember it and speak of it?; इत्य् अर्थः — this is the question intended.
41.translation: The intended question is: how did the boys, at a later time in their boyhood, remember and speak of an event that had actually occurred during the preceding period of childhood?
